state.document: An umpire's account of the state of a battle.
state.sides: prussia and austria; the attacker is prussia.
state.account:
Time 15:29 (149 minutes after the start). Sunset is at 20:11.
States: steady = formed and in order; shaken = formed but disordered or near breaking; in flight = broken and running from the enemy; routed = broken, out of the enemy's reach and not yet rallied; destroyed = no longer a body.
prussia: 32,000 men at the start, 1,875 lost, 29,862 still formed. Bodies: 56 steady (29,200 men), 2 shaken (662 men), 1 in flight (263 men), 0 routed, 0 destroyed.
austria: 41,949 men at the start, 2,131 lost, 37,431 still formed. Bodies: 83 steady (37,152 men), 2 shaken (279 men), 4 in flight (1,361 men), 6 routed (1,026 men), 0 destroyed.

Ground. A side holds a place when it has formed bodies (steady or shaken) there and the other side has none; contested when both have; empty when neither has. 'There' is within 500 m of a village, wood or farm, inside an area of high ground, and within 500 m of a stretch of road. Broken bodies (in flight or routed) do not hold ground.

state.objectives:
prussia (Frederick II): Daun's army stands on the heights south of the Kaiserstrasse between Chotzemitz and
Krzeczhorz, blocking the road to Kolín and threatening the siege of Prague. His left and his
front are too strong to be attacked. His right, at Krzeczhorz and the oak wood, hangs in the
air. The army will march east along the high road past his front, wheel to the right beyond
Krzeczhorz and roll up his right wing in successive attacks from the left, the vanguard under
Hülsen and Zieten leading, while the right wing of the infantry is refused and stays out of
reach of his batteries. The object of the day: turn Daun's right, dislodge him from the heights,
and have the road to Kolín open before nightfall, so that he can no longer relieve Prague.
Defeat that leaves the army intact is recoverable; the loss of the army is not.

austria (Daun): The army holds the heights from the Kamhajek to Krzeczhorz, across the road by which the
King must pass to reach Kolín, and it is the only army that can relieve Prague. Hold the
heights and the road, keep the right at Krzeczhorz and the oak wood firm with the reserve and
Nádasdy's horse, and let the Prussians break themselves on the position. Preserve the army
above all: do not let it be driven down the south slope into the ponds and swamps, and do not
leave the heights to pursue. Should the Prussian attack break, drive them off the field and
away from the road to Prague.
